newsitem.title: FRANCE: France sees cattle aid clouding EU farm meeting.
newsitem.headline: France sees cattle aid clouding EU farm meeting.

text.p: France expects EU farm ministers to clash on compensation for cattle breeders at their meeting Brussels next Monday and Tuesday, a document released on Friday by the National Assembly shows.
Farm Minister Philippe Vasseur told a delegation of European deputies to the French parliament that France was isolated from its EU partners on compensation for veal calf breeders.
France, with 90 percent of total EU calf exports, is pressing for compensation for calf breeders saddled with huge losses arising from mad cow disease, but other EU members are dragging their feet.
EU farm ministers are also to review a European Commission proposal to fund compensation to cattle farmers by reducing aid to grain producers.

Vasseur said the European parliament had not yet given an opinion on the EU Commission proposal. In the absence of an opinion, farm ministers may be technically unable to discuss the cattle breeders' aid plan.
He did not disclose France's position on the proposal to reduce grain producers' payments but he "strongly opposed making reductions in aid to grain producers permanent."
French grain growers last week draped Paris' Arc de Triomphe in black to protest against the EU plan to cut grain subsidies.
Vasseur also said he opposed proposals to have only large grain growers pay for the compensation to cattle breeders.
He said demand for beef had fallen by 15 to 18 percent since reports that mad cow disease, Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), could spread to humans. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
